subject: Social Media
title: Shame as Social Glue
description: One-minute skill: Shame as Social Glue.

hook.text: For 200,000 years, shame enforced tribal norms. Break the rules and the group shuns you. You need them.

buildup.text: In small groups, shame is proportional. Everyone knows the context. Punishment fits the offense.

discovery.text: Online shame has no proportionality. A minor offense gets the same fury as a major one. Scale breaks it.

twist.text: In tribes, shame ends when you make amends. Online, shame is permanent—cached, archived, searchable.

climax.text: We're using Stone Age instincts on Space Age tools. The instinct is ancient; the scale is alien.

punchline.text: Shame evolved for villages. The internet isn't one.

quiz.question: Why does online shame lack proportionality?
